subject: Tenant TTL / Erasure Inventory — mapping & evidence request
messages:
From: Alice Mercer <compliance@ledgerly.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: TTL mapping + erasure evidence for tenant ledgerly-prod-52

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this. Ledgerly is running through our SOC 2 vendor evidence collection and we need the following for tenant ledgerly-prod-52 (prod tenant id):

- Canonical TTL/retention map (per artifact type: prompt logs, KV cache, model artifacts, embeddings, backups).
- Proof of erasure for a recent account purge (we initiated a test purge last Friday) — sample logs, timestamps, and the exact deletion path.
- Policy excerpt or runbook that describes how TTL is enforced and how exceptions are handled.
- Any sampling or attestation you can provide (one-week window is fine).

Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? We have an auditor walkthrough next Thursday and it would be ideal to have the materials 48 hours prior.

Appreciate it — Alice
Alice Mercer
Sr. Compliance Analyst, Ledgerly
compliance@ledgerly.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Mercer <compliance@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: TTL mapping + erasure evidence for tenant ledgerly-prod-52

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can assemble a compact package for your auditor. Plan below: 

1) TTL mapping CSV (per artifact type + retention policy + enforcement mechanism) — attached as ttl-mapping-ledgerly-prod-52.csv.
2) Erasure runbook excerpt + short playbook (attached erasure-playbook-v1.pdf) describing flow, approvals, and controls.
3) Sample purge logs for the test purge you mentioned — Ben will pull a redacted export and a couple of screenshots for timeline verification.
4) Short narrative (one page) that ties the artifacts to our SOC 2 control objectives and sampling approach.

ETA: I can get the mapping and playbook by EOD today; Ben expects to have log exports by EOD today as well. I will compile and send a single ZIP with a brief cover note tomorrow morning. Does that work for your auditor schedule?

Action: If you have a preference for redaction (PII vs tenant ids), let me know — we can provide tenant id mapping or redact the user identifiers.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Manager, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ttl-mapping-ledgerly-prod-52.csv (text/csv), erasure-playbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: TTL mapping + erasure evidence for tenant ledgerly-prod-52

Team — forwarding Ledgerly's request. Ben, can you pull the purge export for ledgerly-prod-52 from 2026-04-17 (the test purge) and include:
- The deletion event log with timestamps (UTC) and the object keys/paths removed.
- Any async job ids and the worker traces if available.
- A short note about how TTL enforcement intersects with our prefix caching layer (where a stale KV may persist).

Marissa/Dylan — if you have a canned one-page narrative that maps artifacts to SOC 2 CC6.0 / ISO 27001 Annex A.18 types, paste it in; I'll include it in the cover note.

Thanks — need to get this packaged by tomorrow morning so Ledgerly has it 48 hours before their walkthrough.

— Soojin

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: TTL mapping + erasure evidence for tenant ledgerly-prod-52

Soojin — pulling the export now. Quick notes:
- Log export for the purge is available at s3://redwood-audit/exports/2026-04/ledgerly-prod-52/purge-20260417.json (redacted sample attached).
- The deletion operation is recorded in the tenant-lifecycle stream and the job id references are present: job-7f3b2a.
- We include a screenshot of the async worker record (screenshot-erase-log.png) and a redacted JSON sample (erase-log-sample-20260420.json).

I'll hand off the ZIP to you when I finish the redaction. Ben

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Mercer <compliance@ledgerly.com>, Ledgerly Security Team <security@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-21T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: TTL mapping + erasure evidence for tenant ledgerly-prod-52

Hi Alice — attached is the package for the auditor: 

- ttl-mapping-ledgerly-prod-52.csv — canonical TTL by artifact type and enforcement mechanism.
- erasure-playbook-v1.pdf — excerpted playbook (runbook) covering purge approvals and verification steps.
- erase-log-sample-20260420.json — redacted export of the purge job showing timestamps and object keys.
- screenshot-erase-log.png — screenshot of the async worker showing job id job-7f3b2a and completion status.

Short summary: the purge initiated 2026-04-17T22:13:01Z, the background job executed deletion passes across object stores and our indexer, and final garbage-collection completed within 45 minutes. We included the job trace and the mapping to our retention policy so you can map artifacts to control objectives.

Next steps: let me know if the auditor needs a live walkthrough of the job traces (Ben can join for 15–20 minutes) or if you'd like additional samples from other tenants for trend sampling.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Manager, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ttl-mapping-ledgerly-prod-52.csv, erasure-playbook-v1.pdf, erase-log-sample-20260420.json, screenshot-erase-log.png
